title: Line Extensions and New Service Construction — Construction Unit Cost Schedule
content:
For **Line Extensions and New Service Construction**, Cedar Fork Electric Cooperative prices new line by the foot, according to the line type built (overhead or underground) and the phase built (single-phase or three-phase), and adds an engineering and overhead loading to the construction cost. The schedule below gives those figures for every class of extension.

## Per-foot line cost and loading

| Class of extension | Single-phase overhead, per ft | Single-phase underground, per ft | Three-phase overhead, per ft | Three-phase underground, per ft | Engineering and overhead loading |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Permanent Residential Overhead Extension | $14.75 | $22.40 | $31.80 | $46.90 | 12.5% |
| Permanent Residential Underground Extension | $14.75 | $22.40 | $31.80 | $46.90 | 12.5% |
| Seasonal Residence Extension | $14.75 | $22.40 | $31.80 | $46.90 | 12.5% |
| Farm and Ranch Extension | $14.75 | $22.40 | $31.80 | $46.90 | 12.5% |
| Irrigation Well Extension | $14.75 | $22.40 | $31.80 | $46.90 | 12.5% |
| Three-Phase Commercial Extension | $14.75 | $22.40 | $31.80 | $46.90 | 12.5% |
| Temporary Construction Service | $14.75 | $22.40 | $31.80 | $46.90 | 12.5% |

The four per-foot figures are 14.75, 22.4, 31.8 and 46.9 dollars respectively, and the loading is 12.5 percent, in every class.

## Selecting the figure

| Line actually built | Figure that prices each foot |
|---|---|
| Overhead, single-phase | Single-phase overhead per foot |
| Underground, single-phase | Single-phase underground per foot |
| Overhead, three-phase | Three-phase overhead per foot |
| Underground, three-phase | Three-phase underground per foot |

The figure follows the line type and the phase actually built on the project, foot by foot: a project with both overhead and underground sections prices each section at its own figure.

## Illustration (hypothetical footage)

A hypothetical 1,000 ft of single-phase overhead line is priced at 1,000 feet multiplied by $14.75, that is $14,750.00, before any other charge and before the loading. The same 1,000 ft built as three-phase underground line is priced at 1,000 feet multiplied by $46.90, that is $46,900.00. The 12.5 percent loading is an engineering and overhead loading added on the construction cost.
